figure_candidates.label: Scheme 1
figure_candidates.caption:
Scheme 1. Proposed mechanism of the transformation of azaspirene (2) into synerazol (1) catalyzed by PsoE and PsoF from the pseurotin
biosynthetic pathway.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 1
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 1. In vitro analyses of the activity of PsoE, alone or with PsoF,
against 5 in the presence of glutathione (GSH). See the Supporting
Information for details. HPLC profiles of a reaction mixture containing
i) the heat-inactivated (boiled) PsoE with 5 and GSH, ii) PsoE with 5
and GSH, iii) PsoE and heat-inactivated PsoF with 5 and GSH, and
iv) PsoE and PsoF with 5 and GSH. Traces are standardized to the
height of the internal standard (IS) peak. All traces were monitored at
l=260 nm. The authentic reference of 5 (v) and 1 (vi) are also given.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 2
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 2. Crystal structure of PsoE complexed with the GSH conjugate
of presynerazol 8a. A) Overall structure of PsoE (PDB ID: 5F8B) as
a dimer. In the first PsoE molecule (left), a-helices and b-strands are
colored in pink and blue, respectively, whereas the second molecule
(right) is colored only in purple. Carbon atoms in the stick model of
the bound ligand 8a are in yellow, whereas oxygen, nitrogen, and
sulfur atoms are in red, blue and green, respectively. Electron density
for 8a in the first PsoE molecule (2Fo¢Fc map contoured at 1.2 s,
green mesh) is shown. B) The active site of PsoE, showing the
interactions between 8a and PsoE. The protein side chain carbon
atoms are in orange. Green dashed lines represent hydrogen bonds.
